counterfactual_missing_items: Repeat bone marrow biopsy: Negative for proliferative disorders
Initial bone marrow biopsy: No abnormal clonal populations
Peripheral blood smear: No peripheral blasts or abnormal B or T cells
decisive_items: Flow cytometry of tissue blasts: Positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117
Transthoracic echocardiogram: Mass within the right atrium, causing restricted anterior tricuspid leaflet motion and mild tricuspid stenosis
response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate that integrates the AML-defining tissue blast phenotype with the right atrial/AV groove mass; R6 captures AML but omits the cardiac localization, while R2 misattributes the blasts to sarcoma and R4/R1 are under-specific. R3 is contradicted by the reactive lymph node FNA.

rejected.why: Too broad; pancytopenia recovered and marrow biopsies were negative, so secondary hematologic malignancy lacks the specific tissue-blast and cardiac-mass localization.
Therapy-related MDS is not supported by recovered pancytopenia, negative marrow biopsies, and 80% tissue blasts with myeloid progenitor markers; the cardiac mass is better explained by AML.
Hypermetabolic cervical nodes are contradicted by normal reactive FNA, and the flow/biopsy findings indicate myeloid blasts rather than lymphoma.
Cardiac sarcoma cannot explain 80% tissue blast cells with CD13/CD34/CD38/CD117; the mass is extramedullary AML/myeloid sarcoma, not a mesenchymal sarcoma.
